task: Replace the per-row ledger loop in read_group_spend with a batched SpendLedger port read (about 100 report filters per SQL statement) implemented in SpendLogsLedger and CutoverSpendLedger, keeping per-row figures and flags identical for the projects-spending, by-users and CLI Insights tables (EPMCDME-17060).

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the analytics read_group_spend helper, the SpendService facade, the SpendLedger Protocol, SpendLogsLedger (enterprise/litellm), SpendLogsRepository statement building, and CutoverSpendLedger. It also needs either a new optional-port-method fallback (no precedent exists) or stubs in Default/Legacy/Noop adapters. Base L (4+ components across handler/service/port/repository), bumped to XL because the shared SpendLedger port contract changes and six-way conformance tests enforce it.

Closest pattern is consumed_for_holders / sum_for_holders (chunked SUM ... FILTER per key, chunk 100, boundary and filter in WHERE, cutover _per_key merge, batch-equals-single tests in test_batched_holder_reads.py). That pattern covers the AccessScope boundary and the edge-case test template, so neither auto-bump applies. Still, no read batches over ReportFilter: per-row users AND projects predicates with alias ORs, personal-project owner pots, a WHERE disjunction of all rows' filters, and per-row group predicates. Failure granularity also moves from one row to a whole batch, and statement-build CPU is known to be high for 100-way FILTER projected statements. Base M, bumped to L because performance is the primary concern.

Source: ledger_group_spend.py, spend_service.py, ledger.py, enterprise/litellm/spend_ledger.py, spend_logs_repository.py, cutover.py, and possibly default_ledger.py, legacy_ledger.py and ledger_registry.py. Tests: test_ledger_group_spend, test_project_handler, test_user_handler, test_spend_service, test_cutover, test_legacy_ledger and test_access_boundary need stubs, fakes or signatures updated, plus a new batch-vs-per-row equality test. That is about 11-15 modified and 1-2 new files across service/analytics, service/spend, enterprise/litellm, repository and tests.

The goal and acceptance bar are explicit: identical per-row figures and the same unavailable/partial/omitted flags. Open design questions remain: optional port method with facade fallback vs. all adapters implementing it, and whether one failed batch may degrade up to 100 rows.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: changes the core shared SpendLedger port contract that all six adapters and the conformance tests depend on
Technical Risk bumped from M to L: performance is the primary concern (30-600 s endpoints, thousands of statements per request)
